st.headline: Australia’s jobless rate hits five-year high in August as more seek work
st.teaser: The jobless rate rose to 4.6 per cent, the highest level since late 2021.
fullText: SYDNEY – Australian employment rose more than forecast in August, but the unemployment rate still hit a five-year high as more people went looking for work, data showed on Sept 24.
The mixed report was not enough to shift already firm market bets that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) would raise interest rates next week for the fourth time in 2026.

Markets have priced in a 95 per cent chance the policy rate will rise to 4.6 per cent. The Australian dollar, however, slipped 0.2 per cent to US$0.7026, a seven-week low after heavy losses overnight.

Net employment rose 39,500 in August from July, when it fell 15,800, data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) showed on Sept 24. That was above market forecasts for a 20,000 increase and driven entirely by part-time roles.

The jobless rate rose to 4.6 per cent, above forecasts for a steady 4.5 per cent and the highest level since late 2021, as the participation rate climbed to 67.1 per cent, up 0.2 percentage point. Hours worked rose 0.7 per cent.
The ABS said it recorded a higher proportion of people who were previously not in the labour force moving to be unemployed.

“Employment growth failed to keep pace with the influx of people into the labour force in August, easing some of the tightness in the labour market,” said Oscar Guth, an economist for Oxford Economics Australia.

“Even so, inflation pressures extend well beyond the labour market, with oil above US$100 a barrel and trimmed mean inflation stuck at 3.6 per cent in July,” said Guth, adding that he expected the RBA to hike on Sept 29.

For August, the labour force rose by 67,700, up 2.1 per cent from a year earlier, while employment rose a slower 1.6 per cent, suggesting the labour market is gradually loosening. That is consistent with the RBA’s judgment that the labour market has eased a little but remains tight.
Governor Michele Bullock said this week unemployment in a range of 4.5 per cent to 5 per cent could help restrain inflation, suggesting some rise might be needed from here.

The central bank has raised interest rates three times in 2026 to 4.35 per cent to tame inflation, matching a post-pandemic high. Yet, core inflation is still running at 3.6 per cent, well above the RBA’s target range of 2 per cent to 3 per cent.

Bullock has warned inflation risks are materialising off the back of the Middle East conflict and a data centre investment boom. With oil back above US$100 a barrel, markets have sharply repriced the global rate outlook, with Australia’s cash rate now seen peaking at 5.1 per cent. REUTERS

cna.headline: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions
cna.teaser: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions
fullText: MENLO PARK, California, Sept 23 : Mark Zuckerberg took repeated digs at Apple during Meta's annual event on Wednesday, only to borrow a page from Steve Jobs' playbook for a surprise reveal: a pocket-watch-sized device that carries Meta's viral Muse AI agent into the real world.

The device, called Muse Charm, highlights a broader shift at the social media giant that has long sought to escape Apple and Google's operating systems with a platform of its own. Users can tap the gadget to access Muse directly, bypassing AI apps on smartphones.

Having once championed the metaverse — the immersive digital world that inspired the company's name change in 2021 — as the next computing platform, Zuckerberg now sees "personal superintelligence" as the bigger and more immediate breakthrough, after his previous costly wager failed.
"It is actually quite clear personal superintelligence will not only come first; it will be much bigger and more important," Zuckerberg said at the company's annual Meta Connect conference.

The remarks follow a blockbuster few days for Muse, which has drawn millions of downloads in what some analysts have said could be the biggest app launch in the US since ChatGPT arrived in November 2022 and kicked off the AI boom.

Investors have embraced Muse's potential to automate tasks ranging from booking flights to filing taxes, lifting shares of partners such as Shopify while dumping companies seen as vulnerable to disruption, including online travel agency Booking and TurboTax software creator Intuit.
MAY APPEAL TO GEN Z, MASS ADOPTION DIFFICULT
Muse Charm could resonate with younger consumers at a time when digital cameras, flip phones and MP3 players are enjoying nostalgic comebacks, analysts say.

Gen Z consumers, aged about 14 to 29, treat AI assistants as companions or brainstorming partners rather than simply search tools. Many interact with technology through voice notes, short videos and AI chatbots, unlike older users who are often more comfortable with PCs and smartphone apps.

"Muse Charm could find some traction among Gen Z and younger consumers. The combination of AI, fashion and personalization could appeal to younger users, especially if it is affordable and easy to use," said Linda Sui, founder of Smart Analytics Global, a market research firm.

The device features a roughly 2-inch (5-cm) screen that can be navigated with a thumb, with a customizable Muse character at its center. A built-in 5G modem allows access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though it cannot make calls.
"They are appealing to people who might not want to wear glasses or might not trust glasses," said IDC director Jitesh Ubrani.

"Some people might remember Tamagotchi and this might evoke that," Ubrani said, referring to colorful virtual pets that became a cultural phenomenon in the late 1990s. "They might be able to run a small language model locally. So you can run AI on such a small package."
Whether Muse can sustain its momentum and the device can amplify that appeal is a question for the months ahead.

Similar devices have had limited success. The Rabbit R1, a handheld generative AI device from startup Rabbit Inc with a screen and a button, had a buzzy launch in early 2024 only to flop because it overpromised on AI features and delivered an unreliable experience.

"I would be cautious about its mass-market potential," Sui said. "Unless Muse Charm can offer unique functions that smartphones, watches, earbuds or smart glasses cannot easily replace, it is more likely to remain a nice-to-have device for early adopters than become a mainstream product."

listening.title: Singapore's Fleet of Electric Buses Grows
listening.transcript: To achieve its net-zero goals, Singapore is actively transitioning its public bus fleet to electric models. The Land Transport Authority aims to have a fully clean-energy bus fleet by 2040. Commuters will soon notice quieter journeys and lower emissions on their daily rides. While the initial infrastructure costs are high, authorities believe the long-term environmental dividends are well worth the investment.

economistArticle.title: You can’t trade your way through the AI apocalypse
paras: Wall Street has fallen head over heels for artificial intelligence. From retail day-traders to institutional giants, investors are frantically bidding up tech stocks, convinced that the upcoming boom will yield endless corporate profits. Yet, beneath this euphoric trading lies a darker, unspoken threat. As scientists and philosophers debate the catastrophic risks of a misaligned superintelligence, a critical question emerges: can the financial markets actually price in an existential catastrophe?

The short answer is no. Standard market strategies dictate that when a risk appears, a rational investor should hedge against it. Traders buy gold, acquire short-term treasury bills, or purchase volatile options to protect their portfolios from sudden crashes. However, if the ultimate outcome of technological progress is a terminal event, there will be no trading desk left to settle the accounts. Traditional safe havens lose all meaning when the entire human financial infrastructure ceases to exist.

Modern risk management is largely built on historical precedents. A financial quant uses past market volatility to calculate the probability of future downturns. But a singular catastrophe—such as a rogue artificial intelligence deciding humanity is redundant—offers no historical data points. Because this hazard is completely unique, traditional risk models are rendered entirely obsolete.

This market failure highlights a broader, systemic issue: the inability of global capitalism to account for ultimate negative externalities. When tech companies race to build more powerful models, they do not pay for the systemic danger they might impose on society. Since the markets cannot organically price the end of the world, safeguarding humanity cannot be left to the whim of traders.

Ultimately, the pursuit of financial preservation in the face of an AI apocalypse is a fool's errand. Instead of trying to short the tech sector or find the perfect defensive asset, society must focus on prevention. The most valuable investment we can make today is not in a clever financial hedge, but in robust alignment research and global regulation to prevent a catastrophic failure before it begins.
economistArticle.cn:
华尔街已经彻底爱上了人工智能。从散户日内交易员到机构巨头，投资者都在疯狂推高科技股，坚信即将到来的热潮将带来无限的公司利润。然而，在这种狂热的交易之下，隐藏着一个更黑暗、未被道破的威胁。随着科学家和哲学家争论未对齐的超智能所带来的灾难性风险，一个关键问题浮现出来：金融市场真的能将生存性灾难折算进资产价格中吗？

简短的回答是否定的。标准的市场策略表明，当风险出现时，理性投资者应该对其进行对冲。交易员购买黄金、购入短期国债，或者购买高波动性的期权，以保护他们的投资组合免受突然崩盘的影响。然而，如果技术进步的最终结果是人类终结这一终端事件，那么将不再有任何交易台来结算账目。当整个人类金融基础设施不复存在时，传统的避险天堂也将失去一切意义。

现代风险管理在很大程度上建立在历史先例的基础上。金融分析师利用过去的市场波动来计算未来低迷的概率。但一个奇点式的灾难——例如失控的人工智能判定人类是多余的——无法提供任何历史数据点。因为这种危害完全是史无前例的，传统的风险模型将被彻底淘汰。

这种市场失灵突显了一个更广泛的系统性问题：全球资本主义无法对终极的负外部性进行核算。当科技公司竞相构建更强大的模型时，它们并没有为自己可能给社会带来的系统性危险买单。既然市场无法有机地对世界末日进行定价，那么捍卫人类安全就绝不能留给交易员们去随心所欲地处理。

归根结底，在人工智能末日面前追求资金的资产保值是愚蠢的徒劳之举。与其试图做空科技行业或寻找完美的防御性资产，社会必须将重点放在预防上。我们今天能做出的最有价值的投资，不是某种聪明的金融对冲，而是对安全对齐技术的深入研究以及全球性的法律监管，从而在灾难性失败发生之前将其阻止。

gems.s: If the ultimate outcome of technological progress is a terminal event, there will be no trading desk left to settle the accounts.
gems.why: This sentence uses a conditional structure ('If... there will be...') combined with a striking, ironic metaphor to highlight the futility of financial hedging against existential threats. This helps learners see how to use vivid imagery to make abstract concepts memorable. / 这句话使用了条件句结构，并结合了极具讽刺意味的生动隐喻，来强调金融对冲在面对人类生存危机时的徒劳无功。这可以帮助学习者理解如何通过生动的意象使抽象概念令人难忘。

gems.s: Since the markets cannot organically price the end of the world, safeguarding humanity cannot be left to the whim of traders.
gems.why: This sentence employs a parallel structure with 'cannot' to contrast market failure with the necessity of external protection, creating a powerful argument. / 这句话运用了带有‘cannot’的平行结构，将市场失灵与外部保护的必要性进行对比，从而创造出一种强有力的论辩效果。
